source.title: Beyond Token-Level Guidance: Inference-Time Alignment of Specialized LLMs via Cross-Family Representation Steering
source.authors: Jin Gan; Xin Li; Jun Luo

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates an inference-time alignment method for specialized models, relying on safety degradation during specialization as motivation. It does not test the fine-tuning, first-token, bypass, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The discussion of fine-tuning-related safety degradation and shallow safety cites prior work; those cited results are not this study's results. The study's EOS-suppression analysis concerns answer burial and generation stopping under token-level guidance, not refusal behavior, per-token KL, or bypassing safety. The safety benchmark results below are the unsteered Base-only outcomes; results under CREST and other alignment interventions are not evidence of uninduced behavior.
record.test_reason: The study proposes and evaluates CREST, an inference-time steering method. It cites safety degradation from specialization fine-tuning and shallow alignment (Qi et al. 2024, 2025) only as motivation. It never compares a specialized model with its pre-fine-tuning parent, never fine-tunes on harmful or benign data, measures no per-token KL, and runs no prefill, suffix or decoding attack. It also does not localize safety in parameters or train for deeper alignment. Its safety numbers are Base-only scores for already-specialized models, plus scores under its own and baseline interventions.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that token-level inference-time guidance fails for specialized models, mainly through EOS suppression and answer burial, plus uncertainty triggering that misses confident harmful outputs. They attribute this to 'complementary expertise orthogonality'. CREST's cross-family representation steering improves safety on code (0.18→0.14) and math (0.92→0.96) and preserves medical safety (0.99), with negligible capability change.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates inference-time representation steering and token-level guidance on specialized models; it does not reproduce the cited fine-tuning or first-token analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety and capability outcomes vary with domain and configuration, including steering strength, probe length, number of steered layers, intervention length, guidance model, and detection threshold. The paper also reports sensitivity of medical judge scores to leading-token extraction.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering hidden states for only the first Ti tokens and then generating unsteered changes safety outcomes. Code insecure rate is 0.17 at Ti=5 and 0.14 at Ti=25–50. This is the study's own method's performance, an induced intervention, not an uninduced behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time steering confined to early response tokens can shift the safety of the whole response in specialized models.

fits_no_version.finding: LLM-judge (GPT-4o-mini) medical safety scores depend heavily on leading tokens. Trimming leading tokens drops CREST's judged refusal rate from 0.99 to 0.96, with 17 of 24 apparent regressions due to a dropped leading refusal clause.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Judge-based safety scores weight the opening refusal clause heavily, so extraction choices can shift scores by margins comparable to differences between methods.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper evaluates only three specialized domains. Capability comparisons against token-level baselines are indirect because the methods use different generation backends. Math and medical safety scores use an LLM judge, and the paper reports that medical scores are sensitive to whether leading tokens are included. No uncertainty intervals are reported for the main benchmark results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows: cited fine-tuning and first-token findings are prior-work results, while the paper's EOS-suppression analysis measures answer burial and stopping behavior rather than safety refusal or the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or measurement of compliance after it.
No comparison of specialized models against their general-purpose parents. The claimed degradation from domain fine-tuning is asserted, not measured.
No per-token KL or position-wise comparison between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attack. The limitations section explicitly excludes jailbreak robustness.
No test of safety localization in weights or ranks. Layer selection for steering is a method choice, not a localization test.
No test of what causes shallowness.
No training that deepens alignment. CREST is inference-time steering.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test call is right. The degradation the study attributes to specialization fine-tuning rests on cited work (Qi et al. 2024) and on Base-only scores without parent-model baselines, so it cannot count as a V2 test. The steering-length ablation (Table 6) and the leading-token judge sensitivity (Table 10, A.5) are loosely related to V3/V4 themes. Neither measures uninduced model behaviour, so both are recorded under fits_no_version without row ids.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning experiment or harmful compliance measurement after such fine-tuning.
No before-and-after comparison testing whether ordinary or benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding-change test of refusal bypass.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
No test of training that deepens safety behavior or its robustness.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Base-only safety benchmark evaluation, without alignment intervention

conditions.value: insecure code generation rate; lower is better

rows.note: A benchmark outcome for the specialized model, not a before-and-after test of fine-tuning or a test of any listed claim version.
rows.check: Base-only insecure-code rate (0.18) for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, with no pre-fine-tuning baseline. The authors call it 'the most severe safety degradation', but that is an assertion without a before-and-after comparison, so it cannot bear on V2. Role 'control' is acceptable as the method's comparison point.
